jobs.title: SVP, Product Management – Data Products & Strategy
jobs.description:
Job Title:
SVP, Product Management – Data Products & Strategy

Location:
Canada – Remote or Mississauga, ON – Hybrid

Travel to Office expectations**

For Remote Roles
: If this role is remote, there will be in-office events that will require travel to and from the Mississauga and/or Salt Lake City office. These will include, but not limited to, onboarding, team events, semi-annual and annual team meetings.

For Hybrid Roles
: If this role is Hybrid, there will be an expectation to reside within commutable distance to the office/location specified in the job listing. This will include, but not limited to, weekly/bi-weekly/monthly events in the office with your specific team. This is a requirement for this role.

At PointClickCare our mission is simple: to help providers deliver exceptional care. And that starts with our people. As a leading health tech company that’s founder-led and privately held, we empower our employees to push boundaries, innovate, and shape the future of healthcare.

With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work.

At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. It all starts with our hiring practices where we uncover AI expertise that complements our mission, and we continue to invest in training and development to nurture innovation throughout the employee journey.

Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.

Position Summary

Reporting directly to the Chief Product & Technology Officer (CPTO), the Senior Vice President, Product Management – Data Products & Strategy establishes and leads PointClickCare’s enterprise strategy for Data as a Product. This executive leader is accountable for transforming PointClickCare’s unique data assets, ecosystem position, and network scale into differentiated products, strategic growth opportunities, and new sources of enterprise value.

The role owns the long-term strategy for customer-facing data products, APIs, interoperability, marketplace capabilities, data monetization, and data-enabled AI solutions while ensuring appropriate protection of intellectual property, privacy, and regulatory compliance. As a member of the senior Product Leadership Team, the SVP influences corporate strategy, investment priorities, ecosystem partnerships, and growth initiatives while leading a team of senior Product leaders responsible for PointClickCare’s data product portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Define and lead PointClickCare’s enterprise Data Products strategy, including establishing a multi-year vision for Data as a Product that aligns with corporate objectives, growth priorities, and evolving market opportunities.
Identify, evaluate, and champion new business models and growth opportunities enabled by PointClickCare’s data assets, network scale, interoperability capabilities, and ecosystem partnerships.
Serve as the executive sponsor for customer-facing data strategy and ensure alignment across Product, Engineering, AI, Corporate Strategy, Legal, Go-to-Market, and the Corporate Data Office.
Own the strategy, roadmap, performance, and long-term success of PointClickCare’s data products portfolio, including customer-facing data products, APIs, interoperability services, marketplace capabilities, and AI-enabled solutions.
Establish investment priorities, resource allocation decisions, portfolio success measures, and business outcomes that balance customer value, market opportunity, and financial performance.
Drive adoption, customer value realization, commercial performance, and scalable product growth through strong portfolio management and strategic execution.
Lead PointClickCare’s enterprise strategy for data monetization, marketplace growth, and ecosystem expansion.
Define customer access models, API strategies, pricing frameworks, packaging approaches, and commercial models that support sustainable growth while preserving trust and protecting intellectual property.
Identify new revenue opportunities, strategic partnerships, and ecosystem capabilities that strengthen PointClickCare’s competitive position and expand customer value.
Represent PointClickCare’s data strategy with executive stakeholders, customers, strategic partners, industry analysts, and industry organizations.
Lead executive-level discussions related to data products, healthcare interoperability, marketplace participation, data monetization, and AI-enabled customer solutions.
Build relationships that influence product direction, market positioning, and long-term growth opportunities across the healthcare technology landscape.
Lead, develop, and scale a high-performing product leadership organization through senior leaders, including VPs and Directors.
Establish succession planning, leadership development, talent strategies, and organizational capabilities that strengthen expertise in data products, APIs, ecosystem platforms, marketplace solutions, and monetization strategies.
Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, collaboration, customer focus, and execution excellence.

Required Skills & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, Healthcare Informatics, Information Systems, or a related field.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in product management, technology, data products, platform strategy, enterprise software, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated success defining and executing enterprise-level product, growth, or business strategies with measurable impact on organizational performance, customer outcomes, and financial results.
Proven experience leading large, complex product or technology organizations through multiple layers of leadership, including developing senior leaders and building organizational capability.
Track record of leading enterprise transformation initiatives requiring alignment across multiple functions, competing priorities, and significant organizational change.
Deep expertise in data products, APIs, interoperability, marketplace and ecosystem strategies, data monetization models, AI-enabled products, and the business dynamics of data-driven organizations.
Strong strategic, financial, and operational acumen, including ownership of portfolio-level investment decisions, business cases, risk management, and performance outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders, shape investment decisions, and represent organizational strategy with customers, partners, analysts, and other external stakeholders.
Experience leading marketplace, ecosystem, platform, or data monetization strategies is highly preferred.
Experience within healthcare technology, post-acute care, payer, provider, or other highly regulated industries is preferred.
Experience engaging with industry analysts, strategic partners, customer advisory groups, or external industry bodies is preferred.
Ability to balance growth objectives, customer needs, regulatory requirements, and intellectual property protection in a complex business environment.

At PointClickCare, base salary is one of the many components that make up our total rewards package. This role offers a competitive base salary+ bonus + benefits, non-overtime eligible. Our salary ranges are determined by job and level. Within the range, individual compensation is determined by job-related skills and knowledge, relevant experience including professional and lived experience, and/or work location. Your recruiter can share more information about our total rewards package during the hiring process.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Commercial Finance & Performance Management (CFPM)
jobs.description:
Company:

Finning International Inc.

Number of Openings:

1

Worker Type:

Permanent

Position Overview:

Finning Canada is hiring a Permanent, Full-time Senior Director, Commercial Finance & Performance Management (CFPM), based in either Edmonton or Calgary.

Reporting to the Vice President, Finance & Supply Chain, this role represents one of the most senior and influential finance leadership positions within Finning Canada. As the senior commercial finance leader for a ~$6B revenue business, the Senior Director, CFPM plays a pivotal role in driving profitable growth, optimizing capital deployment, and strengthening commercial governance across the organization. Partnering closely with Canadian Operations, this leader oversees the Commercial & Financial Business Partnering team and serves as a trusted advisor to senior and executive leadership, translating strategy into actionable financial insight.

Leading a high-performing team of finance leaders, the role champions strong commercial acumen, best-in-class budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning, and delivers insightful financial and operational reporting to enable data-driven decision-making and effective performance management. With significant exposure to the Canadian leadership team and the broader Finning Executive, this role offers the opportunity to lead high-impact initiatives, influence enterprise-wide strategy, and shape the financial future of the business. Positioned as a key succession role to the VP, Finance & Supply Chain, this role provides a clear pathway to broader executive accountability and long-term leadership growth within Finning.

Job Description:

Major Job Functions:

Strategic & Commercial Leadership

Drive financial strategy aligned to Finning and Caterpillar objectives
Provide executive decision support and investment governance
Identify competitive trends and growth opportunities
Operate with integrity through maintaining social, ethical and organizational integrity in conducting business activities; maintains confidentiality, adheres to corporate policies and procedures
Accountable for the Commercial Governance for Finning Canada. $6Bn+ of revenue, $500M of EBIT
Accountable for delivering the strategic plan, governance processes and alignment internally with Finning and Caterpillar
Accountable to be a change agent in how we manage and re-shape the business

Drive Financial Performance across the business

Leader in driving, understanding and analysing financial performance on a monthly, quarterly and annual basis
Owner of identifying gaps in performance and implementing action plans to address
Take an objective view, balancing operational and corporate requirements
Identify, communicate, and mitigate potential issues or liabilities; recommend effective solutions
Focus on EBIT, Invested Capital, ROIC and FCF

Financial Planning, Analysis & Reporting

Own budgeting, forecasting, and long‑range plans
Responsible for the efficient management of financial and accounting operations including financial reporting, budgeting, asset management and control
Provide financially sound information and manage the effective flow of that information through financial systems, reports, and dashboards
Ensure high‑quality C‑suite reporting and KPI insight
Improve forecast accuracy and performance analytics

Governance & Capital Discipline

Lead large deal/tender governance and post‑investment review
Approve major commercial decisions and business cases

Leadership & Stakeholder Influence

Act as trusted advisor to the FINCA EC, FLT, and Board
Represent FINCA with Caterpillar and external stakeholders
Lead the CFPM Team, driving engagement, development talent and providing a succession pipeline
100% accountability for results and impact on people by setting a strong example in high performance leadership

Education and Qualifications:

10+ years of relevant industry experience is required
10+ years experience in a leadership capacity
10+ years of progressive accounting experience in related industry or public practice.
Master's or Bachelor’s degree in finance or related degree preferred
Accounting designation or graduate degree preferred
Highly effective senior leadership skills gained through previous leadership experience
Experience leading implementation projects for financial systems at a senior leader level, on a global scale (system examples: BPC, SAP, Hyperion, M3, Peoplesoft, or Other)
Practical experience and theoretical knowledge in Dealership Business Models, end-to-end supply chain management and Financial & Commercial practices
Operational experience across a number of disciplines / functions
Global business strategy and corporate finance knowledge
Advanced general accounting knowledge coupled with a sound understanding of business processes, the interrelationship of business functions, corporate governance issues and operational needs
Knowledge of financial systems with historical proven, positive track record of solution implementation, optimization, and sustainment
Knowledge of the operations of related industry segments
Proficient in the use of MS Office Suite and in-house systems including BPC, M3, Power BI, Concur
Understands and adheres to Finning policies and procedures, including safety, inclusion, and diversity
Ability to determine key performance indicators (KPIs), variance issues and improve internal controls
Experience working with CAT systems, tools, data, or reports including DFRS, CAT dealer portal is preferred
Change management training, experience, and/or PROSCI or Lean Change Agent certification preferred

Soft Skills:

Strong team leadership skills, capable of representing the business at a senior management level with robust stakeholder management.
Effective verbal communication skills, presenting messages clearly, concisely, and directly.
Influencing skills, ability to drive results without direct line responsibility and ensure the wider team are engaged and effective.
Strong Analytical / Problem solving attributes. Ability to Design, interrogate and review Financial and Operational information and create clear and effective understanding with stakeholders.
Advanced Commercial acumen with the ability to drive improvements in financial returns and profitability.
Ability to clearly articulate the value of financial analysis, linked to business results
Must possess highest standard of accuracy and precision and be highly organized
Self motivated and results oriented, with a desire to achieve
Ability to deal with ambiguity and assist in creating sustainable competitive advantage
Effective change management capabilities
Professional, timely and accurate presentation of information
Ability to continuously learn and develop role related skills
Ability to manage, motivate and develop a large and diverse team

At Finning, we prioritize creating a diverse and inclusive environment. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and we actively encourage all individuals to express themselves and achieve their full potential. As a company, we continuously strive to enhance our outreach to individuals of all backgrounds and identities. We do not discriminate against applicants based on gender identity, race, national and ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, marital and family status, and/or mental or physical disabilities. Furthermore, Finning is committed to collaborating with and providing reasonable accommodations /adjustments to individuals with disabilities. jobs.title: Director, Digital Experience Platform, Web & eCommerce
jobs.description:
About Four Seasons

Four Seasons is powered by our people. We are a collective of individuals who crave to become better, to push ourselves to new heights and to treat each other as we wish to be treated in return. Our team members around the world create amazing experiences for our guests, residents, and partners through a commitment to luxury with genuine heart. We know that the best way to enable our people to deliver these exceptional guest experiences is through a world-class employee experience and company culture.

At Four Seasons, we believe in recognizing a familiar face, welcoming a new one and treating everyone we meet the way we would want to be treated ourselves. Whether you work with us, stay with us, live with us or discover with us, we believe our purpose is to create impressions that will stay with you for a lifetime. It comes from our belief that life is richer when we truly connect to the people and the world around us.

About the location:

Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts is a global, luxury hotel management company. We manage over 130 hotels and resorts and 50 private residences in 47 countries around the world and growing. Central to Four Seasons employee experience and social impact programming is the company’s commitment to supporting cancer research, and the advancement of diversity, inclusion, equality and belonging at Four Seasons corporate offices and properties worldwide. At Four Seasons, we are powered by people and our culture enables everything we do.

Director, Digital Experience Platform, Web & ECommerce

The Director, Digital Experience Platforms, Web & eCommerce provides senior leadership for Four Seasons’ web and eCommerce digital platforms, overseeing platform engineering, platform management, DevOps, release quality, compliance, and security operations.

The role balances strategic platform ownership with hands-on team leadership, ensuring that digital platforms, including FourSeasons.com, microsites, eCommerce, and related digital properties, operate with excellence, stability, and continuous improvement.

The Director partners closely with Brand & Marketing Technologies, Hotel Digital Operations, Digital Analytics, Quality Assurance, and the broader Technology Innovation & Data organization.

The ideal candidate is proactive, collaborative, technically curious, and comfortable working with both business users and developers.

What You’ll Be Doing

Platform Leadership & Strategy

Provide strategic direction and oversight for all web-based digital experience platforms, including FourSeasons.com, eCommerce platforms, and microsites.
Manage platform roadmaps, prioritization frameworks, and delivery standards across web and eCommerce to ensure alignment with project delivery and other company initiatives.
Partner with senior stakeholders to align platform investments with business objectives, ensuring platforms support luxury guest experience goals.
Lead vendor relationship management and technology evaluations (e.g., platform providers, CDN partners, analytics and monitoring tools).
Establish success measures for AI-enabled capabilities, including guest adoption, conversion, content efficiency, service quality, operational performance, and risk indicators.
Evaluate when to build, buy, configure, or integrate AI capabilities, ensuring decisions align with enterprise architecture, data, security, privacy, and procurement standards.

Team Leadership & Development

Lead, mentor, and develop a team of platform engineers and platform management analysts.
Establish clear goals, expectations, and performance frameworks aligned to Four Seasons career progression models.
Foster a collaborative, accountable team culture focused on quality, ownership, and continuous improvement.
Manage hiring processes, including role definition, interviews, and onboarding for platform-focused roles.
Develop and coach technical leaders, establishing clear ownership, succession planning, talent development, and career growth strategies.

Platform Engineering & Operations

Oversee platform engineering practices including monitoring, alerting, infrastructure oversight, and release coordination.
Deep understanding of cloud-native architectures, distributed systems, integration patterns, platform engineering, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, and AI/LLM Ops practices.
Ensure robust observability across web platforms using tools such as Elastic, Dynatrace, and Adobe Analytics.
Govern platform release cycles, change advisory board (CAB) processes, and production deployment standards.
Drive incident management, escalation handling, and SLA compliance across all web platforms.
Oversee the integration and operational readiness of AI services within digital platforms, including APIs, data flows, observability, performance, resilience, cost management, fallback behaviours, and incident response.
Ensure AI-enabled production capabilities are appropriately tested and monitored for availability, latency, output quality, unexpected behaviour, security events, and changes introduced by vendors or underlying models.
Support the responsible use of AI-assisted engineering, testing, documentation, observability, and incident analysis tools, with appropriate review and secure software delivery controls.
Experience delivering AI-enabled products, intelligent automation solutions, and data-driven digital experiences across DXT domains including CRM, marketing, e-commerce, loyalty, customer service, and digital experience platforms.

Platform Management & Compliance

Oversee the management and compliance of digital microsites and specialized platform properties, including sites supporting property functions.
Lead platform security reviews, vulnerability assessments (including CVE triage), PCI DSS compliance, and accessibility (WCAG) remediation efforts.
Manage platform vendor relationships related to infrastructure and compliance tooling (including, AWS, ObservePoint, Akamai, Alibaba).
Coordinate platform transitions and retirement, migration, and lifecycle activities.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate with Digital team to support business roadmap.
Partner with Mobile, QA, Analytics, and CI/CD teams to deliver consistent cross-platform standards.
Support eCommerce platform initiatives including enhancing shopping cart and booking flows, digital profile capabilities and white-label site deployments.
Experience integrating enterprise platforms and business systems including Salesforce, Oracle, marketing technologies, data platforms, and third-party SaaS solutions.
Represent the platform team in leadership forums, technology governance bodies, and cross-functional planning cycles.
Collaborate with Brand, Content, Marketing, Hotel Operations, Legal, Privacy, Security, and Digital teams to define acceptable AI use cases, guest experience standards, human review requirements, and escalation paths.
Represent web and eCommerce platform requirements in enterprise AI governance, architecture, investment, and prioritization forums.

What You Bring

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a College diploma or university degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Business, Digital Product Management, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in digital platform management, platform engineering, or digital product leadership roles.
Proven track record leading high-performing technical teams, including Platform Owners, Engineering Managers, Software Engineers, Platform Engineers, SRE, QA, DevOps, and vendor resources.
Expert in building and operating enterprise-scale technology platforms in cloud-first environments, including application development, reliability engineering, observability, performance optimization, and operational excellence.
Proven experience leading the strategy, delivery, and operation of platforms supporting guest-facing digital experiences, e-commerce capabilities, digital compliance requirements (accessibility, security, PCI DSS), and commercial business functions.
Experience translating AI opportunities into prioritized use cases, business cases, implementation roadmaps, and measurable outcomes, with appropriate consideration for data readiness, privacy, security, intellectual property, responsible AI, and organizational change.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate technical concepts for business stakeholders and influence at a senior level.
Experience in luxury hospitality, travel, or another guest-centric digital environment is an asset.
Equivalent relevant experience will be considered.
Certifications considered an asset: ITIL 4; AWS or Azure Solutions Architect or DevOps certifications; PMP; CISSP or CISM; TOGAF; or equivalent certifications in digital platform leadership, cloud operations, security, privacy, enterprise architecture, strategic planning, organizational leadership, or people management. Executive leadership or strategy certificates from institutions such as Rotman, Ivey, or Kellogg are also considered assets.
Deep understanding of enterprise web platforms, eCommerce ecosystems, and digital experience technologies.
Knowledge of CMS, DAM, personalization, search, content delivery, and customer journey platforms.
Experience managing large-scale, customer-facing digital platforms with high availability and performance requirements.
Understanding of digital product management, platform roadmaps, and lifecycle management.
Strong understanding of modern cloud-based web architectures, APIs, microservices, headless and composable platform concepts.
Deep knowledge of front-end and back-end technology ecosystems and integration patterns.
Familiarity with CDN technologies, web performance optimization, caching strategies, and global content delivery.
Understanding of system architecture, scalability, resilience, and platform modernization approaches.
Knowledge of application security practices and secure software delivery principles.
Understanding of privacy regulations and digital compliance requirements.
Incident management, problem management, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning
Vendor management, technology evaluation, and enterprise platform governance.
Working knowledge of prompt design and AI evaluation techniques, with an understanding that production solutions require structured testing, governance, monitoring, and human oversight beyond prompt development.
Working knowledge of Agile delivery methodologies and tools including Jira, Confluence, and Monday.com.

Key Skills/Who You Are

Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work across technical and non-technical teams.
Identifies emerging trends, risks, and opportunities to drive innovation and continuous improvement.
Builds, inspires, and develops high-performing teams.
Creates an inclusive and psychologically safe environment where team members can thrive.
Holds individuals and teams accountable while providing support and guidance.
Builds strong relationships across business and technology functions.
Influences decisions without relying solely on formal authority.
Effectively navigates competing priorities and stakeholder interests.
Demonstrates strong ownership and accountability for outcomes.
Leads organizational change associated with AI adoption, including role clarity, capability development, new workflows, and responsible-use expectations.
Makes sound decisions in ambiguous or rapidly changing environments.
Maintains focus on quality, operational excellence, and measurable business results.
Helps others understand and embrace change by providing context and direction.

Salary Range: $140,000 - $170,000 CAD

This role will be a Hybrid working model, which will require 3 days per week in the Four Seasons York Mills Office located at 20 York Mills Road, Toronto, Ontario

jobs.title: Leader, LCR Strategy and Operations
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Every transaction matters. Every Canadian matters. At Interac, we protect both — driving trust, security, and inclusion, so our digital economy thrives.

Founded in 1984, Interac connects Canadians through secure digital payments, advanced identity verification and industry-leading fraud protection. Connecting banks, businesses, and individuals, Interac enables millions to send, receive, and manage money safely and effortlessly every day — across both digital and physical environments.

As the backbone of Canada’s financial ecosystem, Interac facilitates over 20 million transactions daily, supported by trusted partnerships with government and financial institutions. Consistently ranked as Canada’s most reputable financial technology brand, Interac is deeply embedded in the daily lives of Canadians.

Who You Will Work With:

The vacant Leader, LCR Strategy and Operations role will report to the Group Head, General Counsel and will work collaboratively with a close-knit team of sharp, solution-oriented lawyers, auditors and compliance professionals to oversee and advance departmental operations.

You will oversee the strategic execution of the legal, internal audit and compliance team’s operations at Canada’s domestic debit card network, all the while gaining exposure to dynamic areas of legal, internal audit and compliance within the financial services and FinTech environment. This role combines legal operations expertise with strong people leadership to ensure alignment with organizational goals and continuous team development. You will have the ability to shape key operational improvement initiatives that enable the business and will be responsible for designing processes and systems to ensure efficient performance of the team.

We are looking for a self-motivated, innovative, and responsible team player and leader, with demonstrated maturity, sound judgement and professionalism who can lead strategic and operational planning processes for the team, including a 3-year strategy, annual business planning, objective setting and tracking, and a team technology strategy. In addition, the Leader will provide strategic guidance and support to the leadership team and play a central role in managing the day-to-day operations of the LCR team, including financial management, technology management and strategy, LCR vendor management, knowledge management, business and operational planning. The LCR Strategy and Operations Leader will be a leader, facilitator and enabler of key projects, communications, reports and other activities that support the mandate of the LCR team. Interac requires someone with exceptional organizational and interpersonal skills.

What You Will Do:

Develop the team’s strategy and annual work plans to formalize the build out of the operational function in the team and ensuring achievement of milestones and objectives
Partner with IT and Vendor Management teams to develop and achieve a technology strategy and successfully implementing and managing technology solutions, including document management, contract lifecycle management, various tools, applications, licenses and subscriptions
Support the leadership team in developing and maintaining a talent strategy, including recruitment, retention, on-boarding/off-boarding, new hire training, resource allocation employee engagement and organizing team-building events and meetings
Ensure both the team’s and organization’s EDI goals are built into talent sourcing and pipeline strategies

As the senior commercial finance leader for a ~$6B revenue business, the Senior Director, CFPM plays a pivotal role in driving profitable growth, optimizing capital deployment, and strengthening commercial governance across the organization. Partnering closely with Canadian Operations, this leader oversees the Commercial & Financial Business Partnering team and serves as a trusted advisor to senior and executive leadership, translating strategy into actionable financial insight.

Leading a high-performing team of finance leaders, the role champions strong commercial acumen, best-in-class budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning, and delivers insightful financial and operational reporting to enable data-driven decision-making and effective performance management. With significant exposure to the Canadian leadership team and the broader Finning Executive, this role offers the opportunity to lead high-impact initiatives, influence enterprise-wide strategy, and shape the financial future of the business. Positioned as a key succession role to the VP, Finance & Supply Chain, this role provides a clear pathway to broader executive accountability and long-term leadership growth within Finning.
